originalRootCause: The generic external-result converter called JSON.stringify on an arbitrary value before rejecting a value larger than 200000 bytes, and the redaction expression was not reliable for quoted JSON secret keys.
revisedRootCause: The generic external-result boundary accepts an unknown live JavaScript value and attempts to make it safe by recursively enumerating and reading it. Because ordinary accessors and Proxy traps can execute during for...in, prototype traversal, property-descriptor checks, and property reads, the boundary can execute external object behavior before schema validation and bounding complete. The affected integration contracts also expose unknown raw transport values to normalizers. The safe boundary must therefore require serialized text or another host-owned inert representation before generic ToolResult conversion; raw transport text must be bounded and parsed by the owning integration before its existing normalization schemas construct supplemental DTOs.

evidence: The failed candidate source directly uses for...in, propertyIsEnumerable, source[key], and Array.map on unknown values.
The harmless diagnostic observed getter, Proxy ownKeys, getPrototypeOf, descriptor, and get execution before the result reached schema validation.

Context7 and shadcn transport contracts return Promise<unknown>; Codebase Memory's injected upstream transport also returns Promise<unknown> even though its production process transport parses JSON first.

The generic converter is exported through src/orchestration/tooling/index.ts and has no non-test production caller found by repository search, so its public internal API is broader than the current live route.

securityBoundaryAnalysis.invariant: No untrusted live JavaScript object is recursively traversed as external supplemental data before an integration-owned inert serialization or JSON parsing boundary.
securityBoundaryAnalysis.selectedArchitecture: Option B with the smallest required Option C transport split: integration transports deliver bounded serialized JSON text, integration services parse and normalize into existing typed host-created DTOs, adapters serialize only those normalized DTOs, and registeredOutputToToolResult accepts only a bounded JSON string.
securityBoundaryAnalysis.whyNotReflection: Object.keys, Object.values, Object.entries, descriptors, getPrototypeOf, Reflect operations, spread, Object.assign, JSON.stringify, structuredClone, for...in, and property reads are not a general defense against arbitrary Proxy behavior. Catching their exceptions would still permit attacker-controlled execution before denial.
securityBoundaryAnalysis.authorityAndContentTrust: Allowlisted Context7 or official shadcn source and local Codebase Memory establish source/transport provenance only. Their text remains supplemental untrusted data. ToolResult contentTrust remains UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL; host-owned project, task, capability, file-scope, dependency, tool-policy, and ChangeProposal authority remain outside external content.
securityBoundaryAnalysis.earliestInertBoundary: The owning transport/service boundary: receive text or bytes, enforce a byte limit before JSON.parse, parse ordinary JSON, run the existing integration normalizer/schema, and only then produce the host-created normalized DTO that the tooling adapter serializes for ToolResult conversion. A caller-provided live object is not accepted as the raw transport representation.
validationLayering: adapter serialization of the normalized DTO
generic ToolResult byte bound, redaction, and provenance envelope
model-context placement as supplemental user-role data

Context7.sourceType: server-side Context7 transport contract; repository has injected and synthetic transports but no concrete HTTP client implementation
Context7.rawTransportRepresentation: Context7Transport currently returns Promise<unknown>; tests and synthetic transport return arrays/objects, so the contract permits arbitrary live values.
Context7.parseBoundary: There is no transport-level parse in the current Context7 service. Context7Service.request passes the unknown response to normalizeContext7Response. Cache hits are JSON.parse results.
Context7.normalizationBoundary: normalizeContext7Response performs Array.isArray, candidate property reads, prompt-injection checks, content cleanup, checksum creation, DocumentationExcerptSchema.parse, and max-excerpt/max-byte bounding.
Context7.currentGenericBoundary: The typed Context7DocumentationPort result is awaited by adapters and passed as unknown to registeredOutputToToolResult; Implementation policy later places typed excerpts in supplemental ImplementationContext and labels them advisory.
Context7.arbitraryObjectReachable: Yes at the contract and custom/test injection level; no concrete network object path is present in this repository. A malicious model or agent has no direct call path to the transport or exported converter.
Context7.requiredChange: Narrow the transport payload to serialized JSON text, enforce a bounded text read before JSON.parse in the service/client integration, then feed the parsed ordinary value to the existing normalizer. Keep cache, retries, allowlist, version resolution, size limits, and prompt-injection rejection. Adapters serialize only the resulting typed Context7QueryResult/ResolvedContext7Library.
Context7.provenance: Attach host-owned Context7 executor identity and tool policy after normalization; do not let returned text set authority or contentTrust.

shadcn.sourceType: server-only official allowlisted Registry transport at the fixed ui.shadcn.com endpoint
shadcn.rawTransportRepresentation: officialShadcnTransport currently calls response.json() and returns Promise<unknown>; synthetic/custom transports also return objects.
shadcn.parseBoundary: The Fetch API parses the official response before the service sees it, with no explicit response-byte check before response.json().
shadcn.normalizationBoundary: ShadcnRegistryService.request passes raw to normalizeComponent, which reads object/file properties, enforces file/content/path/dependency/source-safety policies, constructs host-owned metadata, and parses ShadcnComponentReferenceSchema.
shadcn.currentGenericBoundary: The typed ShadcnReferenceResult is awaited by adapters and passed as unknown to registeredOutputToToolResult. Implementation policy treats registry references as read-only advisory material; dependency metadata does not grant installation authority.
shadcn.arbitraryObjectReachable: The official response.json() path yields ordinary parsed JSON, not a Proxy, but the transport contract and service constructor allow arbitrary object injection by custom host/test code.
shadcn.requiredChange: Use the existing fetch transport with response.text(), enforce a bounded UTF-8 response size before JSON.parse, and narrow the transport contract to serialized JSON text. Preserve official allowlisting, normalization, source scanning, dependency checks, cache, retries, and design adaptation. Adapters serialize only the normalized ShadcnReferenceResult.
shadcn.provenance: Keep official-shadcn source metadata host-owned and separate from ToolResult contentTrust; source approval never makes component text executable or authoritative.

Codebase Memory.rawTransportRepresentation: CodebaseMemoryProcessTransport receives newline-delimited stdout, JSON.parse's each JSON-RPC line, and resolves value.result. The generic UpstreamTransport type currently returns Promise<unknown>, so injected transports/tests can return live objects directly.
Codebase Memory.parseBoundary: Production process transport JSON.parse's the child-process line before the service; malformed lines are discarded until timeout. Persisted cache/metadata also use readFile plus JSON.parse. The current process buffer has no explicit per-line byte bound.
Codebase Memory.normalizationBoundary: CodebaseMemoryService.normalize reads result/content rows, bounds result count and source bytes, creates CodeSymbolReference/CodeRelationship/SourceExcerpt schema values, and returns a typed CodebaseMemoryResult with workspace/index provenance.
Codebase Memory.currentGenericBoundary: The typed CodebaseMemoryPort result is awaited by adapters and passed as unknown to registeredOutputToToolResult. Implementation policy labels Codebase Memory structural data untrusted and never grants write scope.
Codebase Memory.arbitraryObjectReachable: Not from the production child-process wire after JSON.parse, but yes through the public injected UpstreamTransport and custom/test service construction; the generic port/result API is also exported internally.
Codebase Memory.requiredChange: Preserve the serialized child-process boundary, add a bounded line/text guard before JSON.parse, and narrow injected upstream transport fixtures to serialized result text or a host-owned parsed path. Keep existing workspace identity, read-only allowlist, current-index, query, cache, persistence, result, and source-byte policies. Adapters serialize only normalized CodebaseMemory DTOs.
Codebase Memory.provenance: Retain workspace identity, manifest checksum, adapter version, and Codebase Memory provenance as host-owned evidence; none changes ToolResult contentTrust.
